justification: Outreach claims: OC-22 holds on a recorded run; OC-10, OC-17, OC-20 and OC-21 are narrowed to a computed list of councils (DQ-70, DQ-145 and DQ-146 split by council). The public council list drops from 15 to 6 councils.

falsifiable_check.command: python scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py OC-22 && python scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py OC-10 && python scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py OC-17
falsifiable_check.fails_when: no recorded accuracy run exists, the record is under 100 lots, its counts miss the bar, it says passed but the counts do not, or it was measured on different data than is served; or a council that serves a rule read from a plan version we no longer hold is published, or a listed council gains such rows
falsifiable_check.observed_red: With no data/lmr_area_accuracy.json the command prints 'no recorded accuracy run' and exits 1; tests/test_outreach_claim_checks_oc22.py covers each other failure (stale fingerprint, 99 lots, edited passed flag, wrong yes, range, can't-tell). Before this change OC-10 and OC-17 each failed on DQ-70 (957 rows, all in four canterbury_bankstown chapters); outreach_scoped_councils.py printed 'published but fails: canterbury_bankstown (DQ-70 957)' until the list was updated.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The accuracy figure will come from OpenStreetMap's Valhalla pedestrian router, a different engine from ours; this change records it, it does not produce it.

pre_impl.existing_data: No tables read or written. Reads committed data/lmr_walk/*.npz and two data/law JSON files to hash them.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A JSON file hashed as bytes would differ between Windows and Linux checkouts; the fingerprint hashes parsed, key-sorted JSON.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Readiness 17 of 21 becomes 22 of 22 when CI verifies OC-9 and OC-20's jest parts. The what-you-get council list drops to the 6 councils with no unproven, unreachable or stale rule.
pre_impl.frontend_type: The scoped-council JSON now has an empty exceptions list, which TypeScript infers as never[]; the page casts it to a named interface. tsc --noEmit passes.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: None: users never see the claim file.

functions.name: area_check_accuracy_recorded
functions.input: the recorded accuracy file and the current data fingerprint
functions.output: PASS only for a passing, current record of at least 100 lots; FAIL otherwise
functions.if_none: missing or unreadable file is FAIL; a failed import is UNKNOWN

functions.name: data_fingerprint
functions.input: the committed walking files, station entrances and law figures
functions.output: one sha256 hex string covering the walking files, station entrances and law figures
functions.if_none: a missing file raises, so the check cannot pass on absent data

functions.name: no_listed_council_serves_stale_rows
functions.input: the published council list and the per-council stale-row counts from the database
functions.output: FAIL if any listed council serves a rule from a superseded plan version, else PASS
functions.if_none: unreadable list is FAIL; unreachable database is UNKNOWN, never PASS

values.guard_at: int(x or 0) and an explicit re-derivation of the bar from the counts
values.if_missing: counts read as 0, which fails the bar

break_it.scenario: someone edits the record to say passed true
break_it.how: the bar is re-derived from the recorded counts and the fingerprint must match served data

break_it.scenario: the walking data is rebuilt after the run
break_it.what_happens: an old accuracy figure would stand for new data
break_it.how: fingerprint mismatch makes the claim red again

break_it.scenario: a run of fewer than 100 lots or a failing run
break_it.what_happens: it could be recorded as evidence
break_it.how: the scorer writes the record only for a passing run of 100 lots or more

break_it.scenario: a listed council gains stale rows after the list was checked
break_it.what_happens: OC-10 and OC-17 would keep claiming it
break_it.how: the per-council DQ-70 split makes the council unlisted, and OC-10 fails if a listed council has stale rows

break_it.scenario: the per-council split drifts from DQ-70's own count
break_it.what_happens: a council could carry stale rows the ledger does not count
break_it.how: compute() adds a problem and the check FAILS when the split total differs from DQ-70

break_it.scenario: a listed council gains an unproven citation or an unreachable rule
break_it.what_happens: OC-20 or OC-21 would keep claiming it
break_it.how: the council is computed out of the list and the check fails if it is still published

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes: save the GTFS Pathways stops file, run the test step with a new seed, and commit data/lmr_area_accuracy.json with OC-22 flipped to true
